stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on July 16th.
stocks.news:
Stocks pulled back, and the NASDAQ led the way down, off 2.47% to 25,881, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.51% to 7,533 and the DOW eased 0.20% to 52,552. The common thread was a market rethinking a couple of its favorite AI names.

Netflix (NFLX +0.91%) reported higher profits but softer revenue, and told Wall Street it will stop publishing quarterly viewership numbers. Shares are down about 20% this year as streaming competition heats up and engagement cools. Retiring the report card does not usually mean the grades are improving.

Google (GOOG -4.43%) is reportedly delaying its next Gemini AI model because it still cannot code as well as rivals from OpenAI and Anthropic. The update may slip to next month, even as Google plans to spend roughly $190 billion on AI this year. That is a lot of budget to still be running second at the whiteboard.

economy.note: Stocks, the 10-Year, Brent, and crypto are as of the July 16th close; gold and silver are live spot from the morning of July 17th (Market Briefs, Trading Economics, Yahoo Finance).
economy.commentary:
The 10-Year Treasury held at 4.55%, but the louder move was in the metals. Gold just logged its largest weekly drop in three months, easing to about $3,983, and silver slipped to roughly $56.50 near an eight-month low. Gold usually climbs when investors brace for volatility, so this is a change of tone: a firmer dollar and the prospect of the Fed keeping rates higher, with the U.S. and Iran ceasefire back in question, have some traders rotating out of both. Brent crude ticked up 1.02% to $85.09.

Behind the market numbers sits a household one: 42% of U.S. adults say they lean on their parents for financial help. Some economists frame it as a long-running generational pattern rather than a failure, but the takeaway is simple. When parents feel stretched, younger spending slows, and that eventually shows up in the broader economy.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET, July 16th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto drifted lower across the board, with Bitcoin off 0.46% to $63,447, Ether down 0.67% to $1,850, and XRP easing to $1.09.

The real story was in the plumbing. Visa (V +2.79%) is rolling out a platform that lets banks mint and move their own stablecoins, pushing traditional finance deeper into digital dollars. Circle (CRCL -7.69%) fell on the news, since bank-issued stablecoins could chip away at the market it helped build. When the incumbents start printing your product, the competition gets real.

real_estate.homebuilder: Homebuilder Confidence Slides To 34, Matching Its 2024 Low, As Rates And Costs Squeeze Both Sides; Our Live Board Shows 638 Homes Buyers Can Pursue Across Fremont, Hayward, Newark, And Union City
real_estate.commentary:
The daily 30-year fixed sits at 6.68% and the 15-year at 6.19%, both near a one year high, and the strain is showing up where new homes start. The NAHB homebuilder confidence index just fell to 34, matching its 2024 low (see today's chart), as high mortgage rates, pricey land, and costly materials squeeze buyers and builders at the same time. Any reading below 50 means more builders see conditions as poor than good, and the index has now sat under that line for more than a year. Fewer projects at the drawing board today tends to mean fewer choices, and firmer prices, for buyers down the road.

The top of the market could not look more different. San Francisco is riding an AI IPO wealth wave, with some local home prices reportedly jumping from about $2.3 million to $3.5 million in a year as newly liquid tech employees go house hunting. It is the same split we keep seeing: cash-rich buyers at the high end set the pace, while everyone else feels every basis point of rates.
